test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a primary difference between a primary and a secondary electrochemical cell?

options.text: A primary cell can be recharged, while a secondary cell cannot be recharged.
A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged.
There is no difference between primary and secondary cells.
A secondary cell produces more energy than a primary cell.

solution:
The correct answer is __A primary cell cannot be recharged, while a secondary cell can be recharged**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Primary electrochemical cells__ are designed for single-use and cannot be recharged.
 
• Examples of primary cells include alkaline batteries and zinc-carbon batteries.
 
• __Secondary electrochemical cells__ can be recharged and reused multiple times.
 
• Examples of secondary cells include lithium-ion batteries, lead-acid batteries, and nickel-cadmium batteries.
 
• Primary cells are typically used in devices with low energy requirements like remote controls and flashlights.
 
• Secondary cells are commonly used in electronic devices, automobiles, and renewable energy systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Rechargeable Batteries:**

 
 
• Rechargeable batteries are more cost-effective and environmentally friendly over the long term.
 
• They are used in applications requiring high energy density and frequent usage.
 
 
 
• **Non-Rechargeable Batteries:**
 
 
• These are more convenient for devices with low power consumption.
 
• They are generally cheaper upfront but have a limited lifespan.
